mechanism_narrative: A one-week improvement in TRANSIT from -31.3 to -25.0 signals restored commuting and discretionary trips, which raises RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks as transit-dependent shopping resumes.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose 6.3 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT improves by at least 5 points week-on-week but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not higher than the last 14 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -20 percent for the first time in four weeks, it marks a shift from stockpiling to normal shopping routines, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -20 percent from a level below -20 percent in the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -24.1 at t-1w to -18.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -20 but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than the prior 7 days, the threshold signal fails.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT creates a commuting-and-errands routine that multiplies retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC rises over four weeks only when both series improve together.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -44.7 to -37.3 and TRANSIT rose from -31.3 to -25.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve week-on-week but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the last 28 days, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a policy-driven reopening regime where PARKS is positive and RESIDENTIAL falls, reduced stay-at-home orders shift activity toward mixed outdoor-and-retail behavior, raising RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above 5 percent and RESIDENTIAL falls below 6 percent
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at 9.4 and RESIDENTIAL at 5.1 at t-0w
regime_hint: policy reopening with PARKS positive and RESIDENTIAL below 6
failure_condition: If PARKS stays positive and RESIDENTIAL falls below 6 but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not higher than the last 14 days, the regime mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in RESIDENTIAL from 6.3 to 5.1 shows reduced stay-at-home behavior, which immediately increases retail-and-recreation trips over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 1 point week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 6.3 at t-1w to 5.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 1 point but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than the prior 7 days, the behavioral mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Positive PARKS mobility above 5 percent signals favorable outdoor conditions and social mixing, which spills over into nearby retail and recreation spending over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS averaged above 5 percent across all four weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS remains above 5 percent for four weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the last 28 days, the seasonal spillover hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES remaining below -35 percent indicates that office-based demand is still suppressed, limiting weekday retail footfall and pushing RETAIL_REC lower over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES stays below -35 percent for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -37.3 at t-0w remains below -35
regime_hint: partial reopening with weak office return
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays below -35 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than the last 14 days, the negative threshold hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL staying above 5 percent reflects persistent stay-at-home behavior that crowds out discretionary retail trips, so RETAIL_REC declines over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 5 percent for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 5.1 at t-0w remains above 5
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 5 but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28 days, the crowding-out hypothesis is rejected.
